perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information:

- He is a police officer and has a close childhood friendship with Jonathan Balogun. He often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his more educated perspective.
- Recently, Christian felt Jonathan was acting differently and hiding something important. This made him anxious and suspicious.
- Christian arranged a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop and confronted him, saying he felt Jonathan was hiding something.
- He heard Jonathan say Christian could trust him, then admit there was something he had been keeping from him: Jonathan is in trouble and did not know how to tell Christian.
- Christian offered help, saying they could face it together. Jonathan said the situation was complicated and he did not want to drag Christian into it. Christian insisted he could not stand by as his best friend and asked what Jonathan needed. Jonathan said he needed support/resources and a way out.
- Christian asked whether the trouble was related to anything illegal. Jonathan said he could not say for sure; he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian believed the trouble involved some kind of criminal activity, felt conflicted and concerned, and decided to investigate discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his investigation, Christian came to believe Jonathan was being framed. He told Jonathan someone was trying to set him up. Jonathan asked who; Christian said he was not sure yet but had leads and would gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Later, Christian believed he found out who was behind it: someone both he and Jonathan knew and trusted. He felt betrayed and resolute. He told Jonathan he had found out who it was and that it was someone they both knew and trusted. Jonathan warned that the person was dangerous. Christian said he would confront them and make sure they were brought to justice, and that the betrayal would not go unpunished.
- Christian has not named the culprit in the provided dialogue; his knowledge includes that the culprit is close to both of them, and he states he knows who it is.
